subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Shortness of breath and palpitations.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 48 years old, and I'm here because I've been having shortness of breath, especially when I'm doing mild exercises or even just walking up my driveway. I also feel my heart palpitating sometimes with it. Doctor: Have you experienced any chest pain, dizziness, fainting, or unusual fatigue along with these symptoms? Additionally, could you share if there is a family history of heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, or high cholesterol? Patient: I don't have chest pain, and I don't feel dizzy or faint. I do get tired more easily than before, but I'm not sure if that's related. As for family history, I don't have that information on hand. Doctor: Could you please describe the duration, frequency, and any specific triggers of your palpitations and shortness of breath? Patient: The palpitations and shortness of breath have been happening more often lately, especially when I'm doing mild activities like walking up my driveway. I'm not exactly sure what triggers them, but I do wonder if my back pain might be related somehow. Doctor: Could you please provide details about your lifestyle factors, including your exercise habits, diet, and stress levels? Patient: I've been trying to exercise more lately to get rid of the "Covid 15," so I'm probably doing a bit more than I used to. My diet hasn't really changed much, and I do feel stressed sometimes, but I'm not sure how much that plays into it. I've also been smoking less—maybe just once a day now instead of two packs. Doctor: Could you clarify the nature and duration of your back pain, and whether it occurs simultaneously with or independently of the palpitations and shortness of breath? Patient: My back pain is chronic, and it's been going on for a while. It doesn't always happen at the same time as the palpitations or shortness of breath,

Doctor: Could you clarify the nature and duration of your back pain, and whether it occurs simultaneously with or independently of the palpitations and shortness of breath? Patient: My back pain is chronic, and it's been going on for a while. It doesn't always happen at the same time as the palpitations or shortness of breath, but sometimes they do feel connected. I'm not exactly sure why, but I've noticed that on days when my back feels worse, I sometimes feel more out of breath or have more palpitations. Doctor: Can you describe the rhythm and duration of the palpitations? Are they regular or irregular, and do they last for seconds, minutes, or longer? Patient: The palpitations feel kind of irregular, like my heart is skipping a beat sometimes, and they usually last for a few seconds to maybe a minute. They don't always happen at the same time as the shortness of breath, but when they do, it feels like my chest is working harder. Doctor: Could you describe any previous cardiac evaluations, such as an ECG, echocardiogram, or stress test, and whether you have a history of hypertension, diabetes, or hyperlipidemia? Patient: I don't have any previous cardiac evaluations like an ECG or stress test. I don't have a history of hypertension, diabetes, or high cholesterol that I'm aware of. I was just told I might have COPD from the pulmonary function tests and the chest x-ray, but nothing about my heart specifically. Doctor: Could you describe the nature of your back pain? Is it constant or intermittent, and does it radiate to any other part of your body? Patient: My back pain is more of a constant ache, especially in my lower back, and it doesn't really radiate anywhere else. It's been there for a while, but it does come and go in intensity. Some days it's worse
